explain.say: Above an automatic door is a sensor. Many send out microwaves and listen for echoes; when you walk towards the door, the echoes change, which tells it something is moving.

faq.q: How do automatic doors know you are there?
faq.a: A sensor above the door detects you. Microwave sensors notice the change in reflected waves from a moving person, and infrared sensors notice body heat or a reflected beam.
asks: What sensor do automatic doors use?

faq.a: The glass panels hang from rollers in a track. A motor turns a toothed belt that pulls the panels apart and then back together.

faq.q: Why do automatic doors not close on people?
faq.a: Safety sensors, usually infrared beams across the doorway, check that the gap is empty. If anything blocks them, the doors stay open or reverse.
asks: Can an automatic door shut on you?

faq.q: Why do doors sometimes open when you just walk past?
faq.a: The motion sensor sees movement in its zone, even sideways. Better sensors can tell the direction you are walking and only open for people heading in.
asks: Why does the shop door keep opening?

faq.q: What happens in a power cut?
faq.a: Many automatic doors have a battery backup or can be pushed open by hand, and fire exits are designed to open safely in an emergency.
asks: Can you open an automatic door if the power is off?

facts: Dee Horton and Lew Hewitt are credited with inventing the automatic sliding door in 1954.
Many automatic doors use microwave motion sensors that detect changes in reflected waves.
